verses.1: And David went a little further from the mountain. There, he saw a young man standing there, holding bowls filled with honey. On top of those bowls were also hundreds of loaves of bread, as well as a hundred jars of honey and wine.
verses.2: And the king said to Tzibah, “What are these things for you?” Tzibah replied, “The hammocks for the king’s house, the baskets for carrying food, and the cages for keeping the young birds in the garden.”
verses.3: And the king said, “And who is your son?” And Tzibah replied to the king, “Here he is, sitting in Jerusalem. For today, Israel will restore to me the kingdom of my father.”
verses.4: And the king said to the soldiers, “Now, behold, all that belongs to those who are destined for destruction is yours.” The soldiers said, “We will bow down before you, O king, for we see your kindness in your eyes.”
verses.5: And King David came to Bahurim. There, from the house of Bith-shaul, a man came out. His name was Shemiya ben Gerah. He kept coming forward and talking non-stop.
verses.6: And he cast David and all the servants of King David, along with all the people and all the tribes, from his right hand and from his left hand.
verses.7: And he said, “Shimki, get away from this place! Get out of there, you man of shame and disgrace!”
verses.8: The LORD has restored you to your former state. All the people of Shechem, who were under your rule, have been freed from your control. The LORD has given the kingdom into the hands of Abshalom, your son. You are now in your own land again, for you are a woman of blood.
verses.9: And Abishai son of Saruya said to the king, “Why does this dead dog mock my king? Please have his head cut off and handed over to me.”
verses.10: And the king said, “What do I and you, sons of Zeruya, have to do with this? How can I be forgiven when Jehovah has commanded me to curse David? And who can say, ‘I know what you have done’?”
verses.11: And David said to Abishai and to all his servants, “Look, my son has gone away from me, seeking my soul. And now, although he is still my right-hand man, I give him over to him, so that he may be taken captive.” For Jehovah has said so.
verses.12: But may the LORD see me with his eyes, and may He restore me to good under His curse today.
verses.13: David and his men went along that path. Shimei also went along with them, walking on the rocks. He cursed and spurned those rocks as he walked along.
verses.14: And the king and all the people who were sick came there, and they were healed.
verses.15: And Abshalom and all the people of Israel came to Jerusalem. They took him captive.
verses.16: And when Hushai the Arkhyite arrived at Absalom’s house, he said to Absalom, “Long live the king!”
verses.17: And Abshalom said to Hushai, “This is your kindness toward your friend. Why didn’t you go with your friend?”
verses.18: And Hushai said to Abshalom, “Not because Jehovah has chosen this people and all the men of Israel to be under his rule.”
verses.19: And secondly, to whom shall I serve? Not before my son, as I served before your father. In the same way, I will serve before you.
verses.20: And Abshalom said to Ahithophel, “Let me give you some advice about what should be done.”
verses.21: And Ahithophel said to Abshalom, “Go to the graves of your father. They are still there, and they can protect the house.” All of Israel heard this, and they were very pleased that your father had been brought back to life, and that the hands of everyone who was with you were strengthened.
verses.22: And Abshalom broke down the tent from the roof. Then Abshalom went to the tombs of his father’s ancestors, in front of all the Israelites.
verses.23: And all the advice given by Ahithophel during those days, when anyone asked about God’s will, was also given to David and Abishalom.
